> If you expect intermediary fees to be deducted, please let us know which route your bank will take (sending bank name), and share the SWIFT MT103/MT202 advice copy once executed so we can reconcile.

Hi Markus — thanks, and apologies for the delay. Our bank (Banca Lombardia) will likely route via a correspondent in Frankfurt (we expect one intermediary). They won't process an "OUR" instruction for commercial EBICS/EU corporate payments due to local fee policies.

Proposed options from our side:
- Option A (preferred for speed): We will send SHA and additionally instruct a small cover transfer (one-off) of EUR 30 to the correspondent account you provided to offset likely deductions. The cover will reference INV-2028-1187 and should be visible in bank statements.
- Option B (prefer for accounting): We can route via an alternate paying entity (Globex US treasury) who can send OUR, but that introduces FX conversion steps and may delay settlement by 48–72 hours.

We can proceed with Option A if Redwood confirms the correspondent account accepts micro-cover payments and that your AP team will reconcile the two payments against INV-2028-1187.

Also — we need confirmation that Redwood's Ireland VAT ID (IE 349 1234 HI) is the correct one to appear on the invoice so our tax team can apply the correct reverse-charge treatment. If VAT is not chargeable on this invoice, please confirm so we can clear it in our ERP.

Hi Maria / Globex Payments — thanks for outlining options. A few operational notes and final confirmation from treasury / billing: 

- VAT: Confirmed. Redwood Inference Ireland Ltd (IE 349 1234 HI) is the billed entity for this invoice. The invoice line items are B2B services; reverse-charge applies in most EU cases and the invoice does not charge VAT — please apply your local reverse-charge treatment. We'll reissue a clean copy of the invoice with the VAT note and the exact remit reference (attached).

- Correspondent cover: Concordia Correspondent Bank in Frankfurt accepts micro-cover payments. If you proceed with Option A (SHA + cover), please do the following to simplify reconciliation: 
  1) Main settlement: Send the EUR 24,720.00 via your regular EUR rail, instruction flag SHA. Beneficiary reference: INV-2028-1187 / PO-8892; Beneficiary name exactly as "Redwood Inference Ireland Ltd".
  2) Cover payment: Send a secondary transfer of EUR 30 to the correspondent account below with reference "Cover INV-1187 - Globex". That payment will normally post against the intermediary fee bucket.

  Correspondent (cover) details:
  - Bank: Concordia Correspondent Bank (Frankfurt)
  - BIC: CONDEFFX
  - IBAN: DE89 5000 0000 0123 4567 89

- Post-payment reconciliation: Please email a PDF or image of the MT103/MT202 (or your bank's SWIFT advice) to payments-receipts@redwood.com once both legs are sent. We'll match the main settlement and the cover to the invoice. If the cover comes through late or short, our treasury will reach out within 48 hours.

- Small test: If you'd like, send an initial micro-test of EUR 1 with the same routing and reference; our treasury will confirm receipt and advise to proceed. Otherwise, Option A as described is acceptable and will avoid the delay of routing through Globex US.

Thanks — we appreciate the flexibility. I'll have Laura attach the VAT-updated invoice to this thread.

Best,
